site.name: Magnolia Mining District & Rocky Mountain Mammoth Mine Complex
site.location: Magnolia Mining District near Nederland, Boulder County
site.componentDetail: Telluride-gold shaft-mine complex with preserved shaft house and cabin
overview: The Rocky Mountain Mammoth Mine is a historic telluride-gold shaft mine in the Magnolia Mining District. History Colorado identifies it as a contributor to a major mining revival in the district.
Its surviving shaft house and associated cabin form an unusually intact example of the small shaft mines that operated in Colorado from the 1890s through the 1910s.
This point marks the documented mine complex. Access is restricted or closed; view only from legal public routes, and do not enter mine workings or disturb historic structures.

timeline.text: Gold-mining activity expanded in the Magnolia district, and the Rocky Mountain Mammoth became part of the district's telluride-ore revival.
The mine operated as the kind of small shaft mine represented by its surviving shaft house and related buildings.
The Rocky Mountain Mammoth Mine was listed in the National Register of Historic Places as reference 10000422.

moreHistory: The property's importance rests both in its association with telluride-gold mining in the Magnolia district and in the survival of a highly intact small-mine complex.
Historic mining areas can contain unstable openings, deteriorated structures, and metal-contaminated soil or water. Respect closures, private property, and posted restrictions.
